prerequisites: It is recommended to have studied Technical Drawing in high school.

learning_outcomes.text: Know, interpret and use representation systems, their geometric foundation and the standardized conventions and symbols that underpin industrial design and computer-aided design.
Apply their knowledge and understanding to correctly read, interpret and develop industrial drawings.
Understand and use different methods to graphically express ideas, designs and projects in a precise, clear, unambiguous and standardized way.
Carry out technical and laboratory work in computer-aided design.
Select and use appropriate tools and methods to graphically document industrial designs.
Combine theory and practice to solve problems of graphic expression in engineering.
Function effectively both individually and in a team.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability of spatial vision and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and through computer-aided design applications.

syllabus_topics: Standardized representation of basic industrial elements
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, it is necessary to attend and pass the practical assignments. Additionally, a minimum of 40% must be achieved in the final exam score. Specific details regarding extraordinary examinations are subject to the university's regulations.
